en: Add the simulated date to new save file names
Minutes between autosaves, not counting time paused.\nSet to 0 to turn autosave off
Size of body symbols in the 3D view, relative to GUI Size
Speed of the keys that move the camera toward or away from its target
Speed of the keys that move the camera around its target
Speed of the keys that turn the camera (pitch and yaw)
Speed of the keys that roll the camera
Reverse the mouse wheel's zoom direction
Mouse wheel speed for moving toward or away from the target
Speed of left-button drag, which moves the camera around its target
Speed of turning the camera with the mouse:\nShift drag, or right-button drag near the window center
Speed of rolling the camera with the mouse:\nAlt drag, or right-button drag near the window edge
Seconds the camera takes to fly to a new target or view

Resolution of shadows cast by spacecraft and other objects
near the camera. Higher is sharper, but uses more video
memory and GPU time (8192: 256 MB, 16384: 1 GB).
Eclipse and ring shadows are not affected
Fast approximate antialiasing: a cheap screen filter that\nsmooths jagged edges but softens the whole image,\nmost noticeably at lower screen resolutions
Size of text and controls in GUI panels;\nalso scales names and symbols in the 3D view
Hide a body's name, symbol and orbit when the camera is close to it
Size of body names in the 3D view, relative to GUI Size
Language for all text. Automatic follows your\nsystem language when a translation exists
If checked, arrow keys move camera only;\notherwise, arrows navigate GUI controls
Multisample antialiasing: smooths jagged edges on orbit lines,\nplanet limbs and spacecraft. Each step up costs more GPU time;\n4x is a good balance, and 8x is very demanding
Toggle to show names or symbols, or hide both
Show/hide orbits and set their color
Start paused after loading a save

Physically accurate light: sunlight falls off with distance
as it really does, and the camera adjusts its exposure,
so stars and the Milky Way fade out when a sunlit body
is in view. Off: hand-tuned lighting with a fixed exposure
Show/hide points and set their color
Default file name for new saves
Screenshot shape. Preserve matches the window;\nother ratios crop the view at top and bottom or at the sides
Choose a file name and folder for each screenshot.\nIf unchecked, screenshots are numbered and saved\nin the last folder used
Screenshot width in pixels (Aspect sets the height).\nRendered at this size, so it stays sharp at any window size
Size in pixels of small bodies (asteroids) drawn as plain points
Size of small bodies (asteroids) drawn as shaped symbols,\nrelative to GUI Size

Show the clock and date in Terrestrial Time (TT), the uniform
time scale of astronomical ephemerides, instead of Universal
Time (UT), which follows Earth's rotation. TT currently runs
about 69 seconds ahead of UT
Camera will maintain latitude & longitude with respect to the target object
Camera will track orbit of the target object
Camera follows the target object but orients to the ecliptic plane
Locks camera orientation with respect to reference frame: Ecliptic, Orbit or Ground
Temporal antialiasing: reduces jagged edges and shimmer\nby blending recent frames. Experimental: orbit lines\ncan leave ghost trails
